distillation_scope.leaf_granularity: First-layer disease leaf for clinically infected foot tissue in a person with diabetes, spanning infected diabetic foot ulcer, soft-tissue infection, deep-space infection, contiguous osteomyelitis hazard, ischemic or neuropathic wound amplification, and systemic spillover without encoding organism, severity, anatomic subsite, or treatment response into the disease name.
distillation_scope.boundary_policy: Cellulitis, necrotizing fasciitis, primary osteomyelitis, septic arthritis, DVT, acute ischemia, gout, trauma, bacteremia/sepsis, DKA, and HHS remain competing manifolds or downstream/parallel complications when their own observed evidence is present. Culture species, susceptibility, operative findings, pathology, and treatment response are post-workup context, not presentation-only diagnosis labels.
distillation_scope.ranking_note: Presentation ranking should use diabetes context, neuropathy/perfusion context, chronic ulcer or puncture portal, local foot erythema/warmth/swelling/pain/purulence/necrotic slough, ulcer depth, fever or sepsis physiology, CBC, CRP/ESR/PCT, lactate, renal function, glucose, and presentation-time imaging for collection, sinus tract, gas, soft-tissue extension, or bone involvement. It should not require a culture result or final operative diagnosis.

latent_mechanisms.display_name: Diabetic neuropathic, vascular, and immune tissue vulnerability
latent_mechanisms.clinical_meaning: Diabetes-associated neuropathy, microvascular disease, peripheral arterial disease, hyperglycemia, deformity, callus, edema, and impaired leukocyte function create a vulnerable foot where minor trauma or ulceration can become infected and heal poorly.

latent_mechanisms.display_name: Diabetic foot ulcer or puncture portal barrier failure
latent_mechanisms.clinical_meaning: A chronic ulcer, fissure, blister, callus breakdown, traumatic puncture, surgical wound, or unrecognized neuropathic injury creates a below-ankle portal for organisms.
Viable bacteria or fungi in diabetic foot skin, subcutaneous tissue, ulcer bed, tendon sheath, fascia, or adjacent muscle drive local inflammatory signs and delayed healing.

latent_mechanisms.display_name: Polymicrobial, biofilm, and anaerobic wound activity
latent_mechanisms.clinical_meaning: Chronic or deep diabetic foot wounds can contain mixed aerobic and anaerobic flora, biofilm, resistant organisms, and low-oxygen niches that reduce antibiotic effect and prolong infection.

latent_mechanisms.display_name: Local innate inflammation, edema, and pain
latent_mechanisms.clinical_meaning: Neutrophil and cytokine response to local burden produces erythema, warmth, swelling, tenderness, drainage, blistering, and regional tissue edema; neuropathy can blunt pain.

latent_mechanisms.display_name: Ischemia, hypoxia, and impaired antibiotic delivery
latent_mechanisms.clinical_meaning: Macrovascular PAD, microangiopathy, edema pressure, necrosis, and poor tissue perfusion reduce host-cell access, drug delivery, and wound healing.

latent_mechanisms.display_name: Deep-space abscess, sinus tract, and tendon-sheath spread
latent_mechanisms.clinical_meaning: Infection can track from ulcer bed into deep plantar spaces, tendon sheaths, aponeurosis, intermetatarsal spaces, or leg compartments, creating collections that need source control.

Deep or chronic ulcer infection can extend to cortex and marrow, producing probe-to-bone findings, metatarsal or phalangeal MRI enhancement, cortical destruction, and diabetic foot osteomyelitis physiology.

latent_mechanisms.display_name: Necrosis, gangrene, and nonviable tissue burden
latent_mechanisms.clinical_meaning: Ischemia, pressure, polymicrobial infection, and delayed source control produce necrotic slough, gangrene, foul odor, bullae, tissue plane necrosis, and amputation risk.

latent_mechanisms.display_name: Systemic inflammatory spillover and sepsis physiology
latent_mechanisms.clinical_meaning: Severe or uncontrolled diabetic foot infection can produce fever, tachycardia, tachypnea, hypotension, altered mentation, lactate elevation, AKI, bacteremia, shock, and mortality.

latent_mechanisms.display_name: Inactive therapy or inadequate source control
latent_mechanisms.clinical_meaning: Delayed presentation, ineffective empiric coverage, resistant organisms, poor tissue penetration, under-debridement, missed abscess, retained foreign body, or inadequate offloading sustains burden.

latent_mechanisms.display_name: Stress hyperglycemia and impaired wound repair
latent_mechanisms.clinical_meaning: Acute infection and poor glycemic control raise glucose and counter-regulatory stress, weakening neutrophil function and collagen repair while increasing dehydration and hyperglycemic-crisis vulnerability.

axis_couplings.clinical_rationale: Erythema and edema often move together after local inflammatory activation.
Warmth and erythema share local hyperemia.
Deeper ulcers are more likely to expose or probe to bone.
Probe-to-bone raises likelihood and future hazard of contiguous osteomyelitis.
Deep collection commonly needs drainage or debridement.
Necrotic tissue requires debridement or amputation for source control.
Poor perfusion limits antibiotic delivery and healing after local procedures.
Bone infection increases prolonged source-control and amputation risk.
Necrosis and gangrene directly drive limb nonviability.
Gas raises concern for gas-forming or necrotizing soft-tissue disease.
Sepsis and shock are major mortality pathways.
AKI worsens severe infection prognosis and treatment tolerance.
Adequate source control reduces persistent sepsis and mortality hazard.
Higher lactate reflects hypoperfusion and worse outcome.
Lower MAP increases mortality hazard during septic physiology.

effect_modifiers.clinical_rationale: Antibiotics reshape burden only if active against the true pathogen context.
Deep or chronic DFI often needs gram-positive, gram-negative, and anaerobic coverage.
Renal impairment affects beta-lactam, vancomycin, daptomycin, and contrast safety.

side_effects.interpretation: Some broad regimens and severe sepsis increase renal risk.

treatments.context_specific_role: Coverage lane while depth, culture, susceptibility, ischemia, and source-control context are clarified.

effect_modifiers.clinical_rationale: Targeted therapy is strongest when tissue/bone culture and susceptibility match the true source.
Bone involvement changes duration and source-control requirements.

side_effects.interpretation: Renal toxicity depends on regimen and host kidney reserve.

treatments.context_specific_role: Narrowed or organism-specific lane after microbiology context is known; not used as a diagnosis label.

effect_modifiers.clinical_rationale: Debridement or drainage helps when infected necrotic tissue, abscess, or foreign body is present.

side_effects.interpretation: Operative blood loss depends on procedure extent.

treatments.context_specific_role: Procedure lane for necrotic tissue, abscess, foreign body, or extensive infected planes.

effect_modifiers.clinical_rationale: Bone-focused source control matters when contiguous osteomyelitis is present.
Ischemia affects surgical healing and limb-salvage feasibility.

side_effects.interpretation: Minor resection may preserve limb; wider nonviability may commit to amputation.

treatments.context_specific_role: Bone-source lane when imaging, probe-to-bone, or deep sampling shows bone involvement.

effect_modifiers.clinical_rationale: Perfusion intervention benefits ischemic diabetic foot infection more than well-perfused infection.

side_effects.interpretation: Contrast and hemodynamic shifts can increase AKI risk.

treatments.context_specific_role: Perfusion lane for ischemic diabetic foot infection and limb-salvage physiology.

effect_modifiers.clinical_rationale: Amputation becomes a life-saving source-control vector when tissue is nonviable or source cannot otherwise be controlled.

side_effects.interpretation: The intervention itself commits to limb loss when rescue source control is necessary.

treatments.context_specific_role: Rescue lane for nonviable limb segment or uncontrolled necrotic source.

effect_modifiers.clinical_rationale: Offloading is especially important when neuropathy prevents protective pain limitation.

treatments.context_specific_role: Local mechanics and wound-care lane; it does not replace active antibiotics or source control.

effect_modifiers.clinical_rationale: Glucose-lowering effect depends on elevated or unstable glucose context.
DKA/HHS context changes fluid, insulin, potassium, and osmolality handling.

side_effects.interpretation: Insulin can lower potassium, especially in DKA/HHS protocols.

treatments.context_specific_role: Metabolic support lane that improves host repair and reduces hyperglycemic crisis risk.

effect_modifiers.clinical_rationale: Local antibiotic beads or spacers work as adjuncts after surgical access and debridement.

side_effects.interpretation: Local carrier drainage can complicate wound interpretation.

treatments.context_specific_role: Adjunctive local drug-delivery lane after debridement or bone work.

effect_modifiers.clinical_rationale: Shock physiology increases benefit of fluids, vasopressors, oxygen, and renal support.

side_effects.interpretation: High-dose vasopressors may worsen distal ischemia.

treatments.context_specific_role: Physiologic support lane while antimicrobial, metabolic, vascular, and source-control vectors address causes.

Poor control increases vulnerability and delayed healing.

Therapeutic mismatch prolongs infection.

Fever response can be absent or atypical.

axis_response_modulation.clinical_rationale: Mechanical pressure and deformity increase ulcer portals.
Pressure and deformity promote chronic non-healing ulcers.
Delay allows local burden and tissue injury to accumulate.

Delayed control raises severe sepsis and mortality risk.

supportive_care: Perform serial foot exams documenting ulcer portal, erythema extent, warmth, edema, tenderness, purulence, odor, necrosis, bullae, pain trajectory, and weight-bearing limitation.

Assess diabetes context and limb context: neuropathy, loss of protective sensation, PAD, pulses, ABI or Doppler when needed, foot deformity, Charcot features, prior ulcers, prior amputation, offloading, footwear, and recent trauma or puncture.

Use presentation labs to define severity and competing physiology: CBC with differential, CRP, ESR, procalcitonin when severe, lactate when unstable, creatinine/BUN/electrolytes, serum glucose, hemoglobin A1c, albumin or nutrition markers when relevant.

Image when depth, abscess, foreign body, gas, osteomyelitis, septic arthritis, or necrotizing transition is uncertain; radiograph can show gas or bone change, while MRI best delineates deep collection, sinus tract, muscle spread, and bone involvement.

Obtain deep tissue or bone cultures when debridement or bone sampling is performed; superficial swabs, species identity, susceptibility, final pathology, and treatment response should remain post-workup context for presentation-only diagnosis.

Use active antimicrobial coverage, source control, offloading, wound care, glycemic control, and perfusion correction as separate vector fields rather than encoding any treatment as a diagnosis label.
Escalate urgently when systemic physiology, necrosis/gangrene, gas, rapidly spreading tissue injury, deep abscess, ischemia, or altered mentation suggests limb- or life-threatening infection.
Do not narrow this manifold by organism, severity, osteomyelitis status, or amputation outcome. Mimics and adjacent leaves should win only when their own observed evidence is stronger.
quality_notes: No treatment-rank or diagnosis-rank labels are encoded.
Osteomyelitis, sepsis, necrotizing transition, and amputation are represented as axes/event hazards or treatment context, not as hard-coded outcome labels.
